title: Morocco Continue African Dream with Commanding 2-0 Win Over Uruguay
summary: Morocco extended their remarkable World Cup run with a polished 2-0 victory over Uruguay, reinforcing their credentials as genuine contenders.
content:
Morocco demonstrated once again that their 2022 World Cup semi-final run was no fluke, producing a commanding 2-0 victory over Uruguay at NRG Stadium in Houston. Walid Regragui's side were superior in every department, and the result sends a clear message to the rest of the tournament.

Atlas Lions Strike Early

Morocco set the tone from the opening whistle with relentless pressing that pinned Uruguay deep inside their own half. The breakthrough arrived in the 22nd minute through Youssef En-Nesyri, who rose highest to meet Hakim Ziyech's outswinging corner with a bullet header that gave Sergio Rochet no chance. The goal was the culmination of sustained Moroccan dominance, with Sofyan Amrabat controlling the midfield tempo alongside Azzedine Ounahi in a partnership that has become one of the most effective in international football.

Ziyech Seals the Victory

The second goal arrived on the stroke of half-time and was a thing of beauty. Achraf Hakimi embarked on one of his trademark overlapping runs down the right, drawing two Uruguayan defenders before laying the ball back to Ziyech on the edge of the area. The veteran playmaker took one touch to set himself before whipping a sumptuous left-footed strike into the top corner, leaving Rochet rooted to the spot. It was Ziyech's finest moment in a Moroccan shirt and his third World Cup goal across two tournaments.

Uruguay's Struggles

Marcelo Bielsa's side were uncharacteristically flat, lacking the intensity and aggression that have long defined Uruguayan football. Darwin Nunez was isolated up front, starved of service by Morocco's disciplined defensive structure. Federico Valverde tried valiantly to drive his team forward from midfield, but the Moroccan press suffocated every Uruguayan attempt to build from the back. Uruguay's best chance fell to Nunez in the 68th minute, but Yassine Bounou produced a stunning reflex save to deny him.

Looking Ahead

Morocco top Group E with maximum points from two matches, confirming their place in the knockout rounds. Their combination of defensive solidity, midfield craft, and attacking flair makes them a nightmare proposition for any opponent. Uruguay must now beat South Korea in their final group match to have any hope of progression.
